source: Cifuentes et al. 2020, A&A 642, A115 (CARMENES input catalogue, SED-integrated Lbol)
nature: M dwarf (M3.5 V); not a subdwarf by its measured metallicity
notes: IDENTITY: the workbook row is the MSC's component C, which is NOT the star SIMBAD calls 'GJ 644 C'. MSC catalog (J/ApJS/235/6, WDS 16555-0820) component C = 'BD-08_4352C, GJ_643, NLTT_43797', HIP 82809, SpT 'M4VI+sd', 72.2" from AB (systems row: AB,C 'LDS 573 AB,C', SpT2 'sdM4', Mass2 0.2). SIMBAD resolves 'GJ 644 C' to VB 8 (M7Ve, Gaia DR3 4339417394313320192), which in the MSC is component F at 232" (WNO 55 AB,F, 0.09 Msun). So: workbook GJ 644 C = GJ 643 = Wolf 629 = HD 152751C (SIMBAD main id) = Gaia DR3 4339465360510320128; SIMBAD type M3.5V (Kirkpatrick et al. 1991). The 'sdM4'/'M4VI+sd' class is the MSC's legacy label; measured metallicities are near-solar to mildly poor ([Fe/H] -0.26 Mann+2015, -0.05 Schweitzer+2019, Gaia GSP-Phot -0.79), and every modern source treats it as a main-sequence M3.5 dwarf. Consider renaming the row to GJ 643 to avoid the clash with vB 8. AGREEING VALUES for GJ 643: Schweitzer et al. 2019 A&A 625, A68 (J/A+A/625/A68, Gl 643): 'Lum 5.720e-03 8.60e-05', Teff 3345, R 0.2251, d 6.497 pc; Mann et al. 2015 ApJ 804, 64 (J/ApJ/804/64, Gl 643): Fbol 0.4005e-8 erg/s/cm2, Teff 3279, R 0.233 -> R^2(T/5772)^4 = 5.65e-3; Hardegree-Ullman et al. 2023 AJ 165, 267 (Wolf 629): L 5.38e-3 +/- 1.6e-4; TIC v8.2 181589885: 6.10e-3 +/- 1.5e-3. Gaia DR3 FLAME (6.05e-3, flag 20) has bounds 1.000e-2..1.105e-2 that do not bracket the value -- not used. DISTANCE: source uses 6.497 pc (Gaia DR2 plx 153.92 of C itself); workbook 20.96 ly = 6.43 pc (HIP plx 155.6 of A) -> rescaling would multiply by 0.978 (5.28e-3). For reference only, VB 8 (the SIMBAD 'GJ 644 C'): Cifuentes 2020 Lbol 6.067e-4 +/- 6.1e-6, M7.0 V.

nature: M dwarf if real; existence as a body separate from the SB2 secondary (MSC Bb) is doubtful
notes: No photometry of C on its own exists, so no L can be split out. MSC (J/ApJS/235/6) has B,C 'v,a' 1.33" P 98.8 yr citing '2003 AJ 125 332' = Jao et al. 2003 (Solar Neighborhood VII, doi:10.1086/345515; both CD-32 13297 and 13298 are in its SIMBAD object list), and separately Ba,Bb 's2,a' (Delfosse et al. 1999 SB2) with V 11.87/12.87. The MSC notes for 17462-3206 read: 'HST observations of BC. C is not in DR3.' (2012AJ....144...64D) and 'Believe B is SB2. V(ABC)=(10.50,11.87,12.87), masses=(0.49,0.33,0.25)' (2019AJ....157..216W). Checked: (1) Winters et al. 2019 AJ 157, 216 (J/AJ/157/216 tables 4, 11) count GJ 2130 as a TRIPLE (Nsys 3): A, and BC an SB2 ('BC < 1.0" 1998 SB2'); their deblended V of C (12.87) carries f_dV = 'b' = 'An assumption was made regarding the dV mag', i.e. no measured split. Their 'C' is the SB2 secondary, which the MSC calls Bb. (2) Dieterich et al. 2012 AJ 144, 64 (HST/NICMOS, J/AJ/144/64 table2): 'GJ 2130BC ... F180 6.75 ... b,c,g', note c = 'Sensitivity measured around unresolved or very close binary' -- no 1.33" companion resolved by HST. (3) Gaia DR3: no source within ~5" of B (4055584308787727488, G 10.28, RUWE 3.53) other than G>20.6 background objects; WDS has only LDS 611 AB (21"). (4) Jao et al. 2003 tables are behind IOP and U. Chile bot walls, not read. CONCLUSION: the 1.33" C is very likely the same star as the SB2 secondary Bb, double-counted by the MSC; Gaia and HST show no third body. Blended light for reference: Hardegree-Ullman et al. 2023 (J/AJ/165/267) 'CD-32 13298' (Ba+Bb[+C]) Teff 3327, L 2.82e-2 +/- 7.7e-4 at 14.14 pc; TIC 111265985 L 0.02396.

source: Hardegree-Ullman et al. 2023, AJ 165, 267 (blend L of L 10-21 B = Ba+Bb) split with Tokovinin et al. 2024, AJ 168, 28 (SOAR 2023, Ba,Bb delta-I 2.5, tentative) and the Pecaut & Mamajek dwarf sequence (EEM v2022.04.16)
identifier: 2023AJ....165..267H, VizieR J/AJ/165/267; 2024AJ....168...28T, VizieR J/AJ/168/28/table1; Pecaut & Mamajek 2013 ApJS 208, 9 (EEM table)
derivation: L(Ba)+L(Bb) = 1.95e-2 Lsun (H-U 2023, unresolved B; Gaia DR3 6350952476849650432 is B alone, 2" from A, but holds both Ba and Bb). Delta-I(Ba,Bb) = 2.5 mag (Tokovinin+2024, flagged ':' tentative; WDS gives the same: Ba,Bb 11.80/14.30). Converting I-band contrast to bolometric with the EEM dwarf sequence (M_Ic = Mv - (V-Ic) vs logL, interpolated): solve L(M_I)+L(M_I+2.5) = 1.95e-2 -> Ba M_I 8.66 (~M3V, L 0.0171), Bb M_I 11.16 (~M5V, L 0.00238). Check: implied combined M_G ~9.9 matches observed M_G(B) = 11.654 - 5log10(100/45.13) = 9.93. Range [0.00186, 0.00303] spans L_blend +/- 1 sigma and delta-I 2.2-2.8.
nature: M dwarf (~M5 V by its contrast; workbook mass 0.153 assumed)
notes: Low confidence: the Ba,Bb resolution itself is tentative (one SOAR epoch, ':' on delta-m) and the blend L has no K-band input (H-U list no Ks for B). TIC v8.2 2054524454 has no L; Gaia FLAME none. SOAR also gives Aa,B dI 3.4 at 2.12", which disagrees with Gaia's dG(A,B) 2.19 (speckle dm at 2" is unreliable) -- not used. DISTANCE: H-U used 22.39 pc (B's own plx 44.67); workbook 72.27 ly = 22.16 pc (A's plx 45.13) -> rescaling would multiply by 0.980 (0.00233). Ba by the same split ~0.0171 (not asked).

source: Hardegree-Ullman et al. 2023, AJ 165, 267 (L of the unresolved C = L 347-73), minus a nominal Cb from the Pecaut & Mamajek dwarf sequence
derivation: L(C blend) = 1.64e-2 +/- 6.5e-4 Lsun (H-U 2023; blend mass 0.389, matching the workbook's Ca 0.30 + Cb 0.09). Cb has no photometry; taking it as the workbook's 0.09 Msun dwarf, EEM gives M7V (Msun 0.090) logL -3.19 -> 6.5e-4 Lsun. L(Ca) = 0.0164 - 0.00065 = 0.0157. Upper bound 0.0170 (blend +1 sigma, Cb dark); lower bound 0.0082 (equal-light pair).
nature: M dwarf (~M2.5-M3 V; Teff 3423 K for the blend)
notes: The blend value is published; the Ca/Cb split is not -- Cb is hypothetical (MSC 'a,v?', 'RUWE=21.2 fdbl=52'), so the subtraction rests on the workbook's own assumed Cb mass. Gaia DR3 ipd_frac_multi_peak = 52 (a double peak in half the scans) hints Cb may be brighter than a 0.09 Msun dwarf, which would push Ca toward the lower bound. TIC 424876997 (L 0.01739) has no Teff and rests on a 43.8 pc distance -- not used. Gaia FLAME: none. DISTANCE: H-U used 27.50 pc (C's own plx 36.41, RUWE 21); workbook 87.21 ly = 26.74 pc (A's plx 37.4) -> rescaling multiplies by 0.945 (0.0148).

source: Hardegree-Ullman et al. 2023, AJ 165, 267 (L of unresolved WT 50 = Ba+Bb) split with Tokovinin et al. 2024, AJ 168, 28 (SOAR delta-I 0.2) and the Pecaut & Mamajek dwarf sequence
derivation: L(Ba)+L(Bb) = 6.23e-3 +/- 1.9e-4 Lsun (H-U 2023, unresolved WT 50, Teff 3170, dist 17.40 pc). Delta-I = 0.2 (Tokovinin+2024, tentative ':'; WDS TSN 9001 Ba,Bb mags 13.20/13.40 agree). Via the EEM sequence (M_Ic vs logL near M4.5V): L(M_I)+L(M_I+0.2) = 6.23e-3 -> Ba 3.36e-3, Bb 2.87e-3. Simple delta-mbol = delta-I gives 3.40e-3 / 2.83e-3. Range covers L +/- 1 sigma and delta-I 0.0-0.4.
notes: Blend contains Ba+Bb only (0.03" pair; RUWE 3.32). TIC v8.2 229142295: L 6.15e-3, Teff 3131, R 0.267 for the blend -- agrees within 1.3%. Gaia DR3 FLAME: none. Distance: H-U 17.40 pc vs workbook 56.54 ly = 17.34 pc -> factor 0.993, negligible.
